articles.title: Humpback whale mother may have mourned her dead calf for days
articles.summary: Researchers observed a humpback whale mother staying beside her presumed stillborn calf for hours and possibly days off Australia’s Gold Coast. She maintained eye contact and remained close to the calf in behavior resembling caregiving and nurturing. Scientists say the rare observation may provide new insight into grief, maternal attachment, and emotional complexity in humpback whales.
articles.content:
A rare observation of a humpback whale mother remaining beside her dead calf is offering researchers a closer look at how these animals may respond to loss.

The encounter, documented by researchers from Griffith University and Sea World Foundation, raises the possibility that humpback whale mothers may experience grief when a calf dies.

In 2025, a female humpback whale was observed off the southern Gold Coast with an escort whale after apparently giving birth to a deceased calf. The mother stayed near the calf for several hours and may have remained with it for days.

[See link to video below article.]

Rare Death-Related Behavior in Humpback Whales

Dr. Olaf Meynecke, from Griffith University's Whales and Climate Research Program, said attentive behavior toward dead individuals has been recorded mainly in toothed whales and delphinids (known as odontocetes). Similar observations remain far less common in published research involving baleen whales such as humpbacks.

"Unlike reports of toothed whales where mothers have been observed lifting their dead calves to the surface, this humpback whale mother showed prolonged post-mortem behavior and attention towards her deceased calf under the surface," Dr. Meynecke said.

"She remained close to the calf, maintaining eye contact and positioning herself next to her calf over several hours and maybe even days.

"These observed behaviors were consistent with care-giving or nurturing actions and post-mortem attentive responses documented in socially complex mammals, and indicated an inherent, strong maternal attachment to the calf."

Cetaceans are among the most widely recognized and closely watched marine animals, regularly attracting significant public attention.

An Unexpected Encounter at Sea

Sea World Foundation Rescue Boat Captain Andrew Mulville witnessed the unusual interaction firsthand.

"When I actually worked out what was happening, I was totally surprised."

"At first sight, I thought it was just two whales resting on the surface, but their behavior was unusual.

"It was definitely not what I was expecting to see out at sea that day."

The observation adds to the small number of documented cases involving deceased calves in baleen whales. According to Dr. Meynecke, these rare and deeply sad encounters could help scientists better understand how large whales process death and what their behavior may reveal about cognition and emotion.

What Whale Behavior May Reveal About Grief

Because such events are rarely witnessed, researchers say careful documentation is important for determining whether these behaviors reflect maternal attachment, grief-like responses, or other forms of social and emotional behavior.

"This case study highlights the need for continued systematic documentation of rare neonatal mortality events to better understand the cognitive, emotional, and evolutionary significance of post-mortem behavior in large whales," he said.

"Understanding how non-human animals responded to death provides insight into their emotional lives, social bonds, and cognitive capacities."

The study, 'First documentation of humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) post-mortem attendance of a stillborn,' has been published in Discover Animals.

articles.personality_title: Humpback whale mother stays close to her stillborn calf, showing signs of grief
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Researchers have rarely seen how large whales react when a calf dies. Most observations of grief-like behavior in whales come from smaller, toothed whales, not the bigger baleen whales like humpbacks.

**What happened** – In 2025, near Australia’s Gold Coast, scientists watched a humpback whale mother stay beside her dead calf for many hours, possibly days. She kept eye contact and stayed very close, acting as if she was caring for the calf even after it had died.

**Impact** – This rare behavior shows that humpback whales might feel strong emotions like grief and have deep bonds with their young. It gives scientists new clues about how smart and emotionally complex these large whales are, something not well understood before.

**What's next step** – Researchers want to keep studying these rare events to learn more about whale emotions and social bonds. By watching and recording similar cases, they hope to understand how whales think and feel, especially about loss.

**One-sentence takeaway** – A humpback whale mother’s unusual care for her dead calf reveals new insights into whale emotions and maternal bonds.
articles.personality_title_fr: Une mère baleine à bosse reste près de son veau mort, montrant des signes de deuil
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les chercheurs ont rarement observé comment les grandes baleines réagissent lorsqu’un veau meurt. La plupart des comportements proches du deuil ont été vus chez des petites baleines à dents, pas chez les grandes baleines à fanons comme les baleines à bosse.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – En 2025, près de la Gold Coast en Australie, des scientifiques ont vu une mère baleine à bosse rester à côté de son veau mort pendant plusieurs heures, peut-être plusieurs jours. Elle a gardé un contact visuel et est restée très proche, comme si elle s’occupait encore du veau.

**Impact** – Ce comportement rare montre que les baleines à bosse pourraient ressentir des émotions fortes comme le deuil et avoir des liens profonds avec leurs petits. Cela donne aux scientifiques de nouvelles idées sur l’intelligence et la complexité émotionnelle de ces grandes baleines, peu comprises jusqu’ici.

**Prochaine étape** – Les chercheurs veulent continuer à étudier ces événements rares pour mieux comprendre les émotions et les liens sociaux des baleines. En observant et enregistrant d’autres cas, ils espèrent découvrir comment les baleines pensent et ressentent, surtout face à la perte.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le soin inhabituel d’une mère baleine à bosse pour son veau mort révèle de nouvelles informations sur les émotions et les liens maternels chez les baleines.
articles.personality_title_es: Madre de ballena jorobada permanece junto a su cría muerta, mostrando señales de duelo
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los investigadores rara vez han visto cómo reaccionan las grandes ballenas cuando una cría muere. La mayoría de los comportamientos que parecen de duelo se han observado en ballenas dentadas pequeñas, no en las grandes ballenas barbadas como las jorobadas.

**Qué pasó** – En 2025, cerca de la Costa Dorada en Australia, científicos observaron a una madre ballena jorobada que se quedó junto a su cría muerta durante varias horas, posiblemente días. Mantuvo contacto visual y se mantuvo muy cerca, como si siguiera cuidando a la cría.

**Impacto** – Este comportamiento raro muestra que las ballenas jorobadas podrían sentir emociones fuertes como el duelo y tener vínculos profundos con sus crías. Esto da nuevas pistas sobre la inteligencia y la complejidad emocional de estas grandes ballenas, algo poco conocido hasta ahora.

**Próximo paso** – Los investigadores quieren seguir estudiando estos eventos raros para entender mejor las emociones y los lazos sociales de las ballenas. Al observar y documentar casos similares, esperan aprender cómo piensan y sienten las ballenas, especialmente ante la pérdida.

**Resumen en una frase** – El cuidado inusual de una madre ballena jorobada por su cría muerta ofrece nuevas ideas sobre las emociones y los lazos maternos en las ballenas.
